catalysts.headline: NVIDIA announced Jensen Huang resigned as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately, following reports of personal relationships -- including one with a woman US intelligence agencies reportedly suspect of spying for China. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO; Harvey C. Jones was named the company's first-ever board chair. Kress is to lead a search for a permanent CEO considering internal and external candidates. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC the board decided to oust Huang the previous night.
catalysts.impact: Shares fell sharply but sources disagree sharply on magnitude -- see conflicts

catalysts.headline: NVDA fell ~5.48% premarket to $176.41, flagged among the day's weakest S&P 500 premarket names, continuing the AI/chip-stock weakness that produced the 2026-11-05 selloff already on file.
NVDA closed at $178.67, down 4.27% ($7.97) in the US session, as the board's independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang (disclosed Nov 8) continued to weigh on shares

NVIDIA's board launched an independent investigation, overseen by independent directors with outside counsel, into reports (originating from a late-October New York Times article) that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of an alleged Chinese intelligence effort via a personal relationship with Alice Huang (aka Huang Le), a former Megaspeed International executive; the board said it has no reason to believe national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised but would examine all available information, and reaffirmed support for Huang, who remains CEO; three House Republican committee chairs requested a closed-door briefing from Huang on Nov. 18; claims that the individual worked for China's Ministry of State Security or was involved in chip smuggling are unconfirmed and denied by Beijing
catalysts.impact: Cited as the primary driver of a multi-day NVDA selloff culminating in the stock's worst 5-day stretch since 2022 and its worst day versus the S&P 500 since the Jan 2025 DeepSeek shock

catalysts.headline: NVDA fell 9.26% to close at $181.60 (from $200.13 on 2026-11-04), its largest single-session decline in the trailing 365 days, as a broad AI/chip-stock selloff hit the sector amid post-midterm-election concern over political risk to AI data-center buildout; the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% (to 24,315.00) and the S&P 500 fell 4.4% (to 7,353.73) the same session, erasing roughly $3 trillion in market value market-wide.
NVIDIA confirmed it will report fiscal Q3 2027 results (quarter ended 2026-10-25) via a conference call on 2026-11-17 at 2:00pm PT / 5:00pm ET
catalysts.impact: Confirms the upcoming earnings date, which falls after this report's date (2026-11-13)
